questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Argument of a Complex Number in the Second Quadrant
questions.problem:
Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=-3+4\text{i}.$ 

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13929099/assets/373ea8254a9816f67bfbcaf993348f409c1047284d09c43e5d41e68b15c5af58.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\frac{\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<\pi .$ If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{4}{3} \\ \alpha  & =arctan⁡(\frac{4}{3}) \\  & ≈0.927\,30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)≈\pi -0.927\,30≈2.21
$$

to two decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Argument of a Complex Number in the Fourth Quadrant
questions.problem:
Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=7-5\text{i}.$ 

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13929099/assets/d096d76118bc06b2d5c79d5017c0178d96fc84bff6f97d563b7b872d26e75d20.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\frac{3\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<2\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the positive real axis, then

$$
\alpha =arctan⁡(\frac{5}{7})≈0.620\,25.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=2\pi -0.620\,25≈5.66
$$

to two decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Argument of a Complex Number in the Fourth Quadrant
questions.problem:
Find, **in radians**, the **exact value** of the argument of $z=8\sqrt{3}-8\text{i}.$

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$arg⁡(z)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13929099/assets/78399e67e0ba69c1d7848a41aa5d4a5f8040fc578aab30a99f7e19ac86ece179.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{3\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<2\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the positive real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{8}{8\sqrt{3}} \\ \alpha  & =arctan\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{11\pi }{6}.
$$
